about.title: Woodlake Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Woodlake sits in the citrus country of Tulare County, a town of about 7,654 people where the loss of a neighbor is felt on every block. When a death happens because someone else was careless — on Avenue 344, along Valencia Boulevard, on Rt 216 or Main Street, at a job site, or in a care setting — California law gives certain family members a way to hold the responsible party accountable in civil court. That claim runs on its own track, whether or not prosecutors ever file charges. Public records show Woodlake reported no traffic deaths in 2025, and we hope that holds. Still, wrongful death claims arise from far more than crashes, and the two-year deadline (shorter when a public agency is involved) does not pause while a family grieves. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that listens to what happened and connects you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Woodlake Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We help sort out who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim — a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can explain where your family fits.

items.title: The clock is real, and we respect it
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter if a city, county, or state agency is involved. Reaching out early protects your options.

items.title: No cost to connect, no fee without recovery
items.desc: LawProactive is free, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. Losses such as funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance can all be part of the claim.

items.question: Public records show no traffic deaths in Woodlake in 2025. Does a wrongful death claim still apply here?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is not limited to crashes on Avenue 344 or Rt 216. It can arise from workplace incidents, medical or nursing-home neglect, defective products, or unsafe property anywhere in Tulare County. If someone's carelessness caused a death, the civil law applies regardless of local crash counts.

items.question: The other person is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, completely separate from any criminal case brought by the Tulare County District Attorney. You can pursue it whether or not charges are filed, and even if a criminal case ends without a conviction. Waiting can put your two-year deadline at risk, so it is worth talking to an attorney soon.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The value of each claim depends on the specific facts, and no outcome can be promised. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain what is realistic for your family.
